statements.text: I’m committed to working with Republicans and Democrats to brainstorm common sense solutions to issues in the age of AI!

This legislation isn't just about technology - it's about building an economy and a future that works for everyone, from Silicon Valley all the way to Main Street. As AI creates new industries, reshapes old ones, and redefines the skills people need to succeed, this bill will make sure small businesses aren't being left behind.
statements.venue: Joint press release introducing AI for Main Street Act

statements.text: The AI WISE Act directs SBA to establish educational resources on AI for small businesses through its online learning program.
statements.context: Remarks during a House Small Business Committee markup of multiple bills, including the AI-WISE Act, which directs SBA to create AI educational resources for small businesses.

statements.text: The AI WISE Act requires the SBA to create AI literacy resources tailored specifically to small businesses.
statements.context: House Small Business Committee markup of multiple bills including the AI-WISE Act.

statements.text: In our increasingly connected world, AI presents major changes to our economy and our way of life, from streamlining bookkeeping to managing inventory to improving customer outreach. AI can help small businesses save time, cut cost, stay competitive, but only if they have the knowledge how to use it effectively.
statements.context: House Small Business Committee markup of multiple bills including the AI for Main Street Act.

statements.text: Today, my AI Wise Act passed out of the Small Business Committee. It’s commonsense, bipartisan legislation that would make sure small businesses have the resources they need to harness the power of AI - and avoid its pitfalls. https://t.co/7M2rEOQH1M

After my AI WISE Act passed through committee, I met with industry leaders from OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft to talk about how AI will impact West Michigan’s local economy.

We need to make sure innovation supports workers and small businesses. https://t.co/6ySTNWT5cb
My bill, the AI-WISE Act, would help to educate small businessowners on those risks. [...] I am so proud of the bipartisan support that bill has received in this Committee.
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled "Main Street Under Attack: The Cost of Crime on Small Businesses," where Rep. Scholten questions a witness and highlights her own bill.

statements.text: At this week’s Small Business Committee hearing, I had the opportunity to question Ms. Lisa Plaggemier about AI and cybersecurity and what small businesses need to stay protected. My AI-WISE Act would require the Small Business Administration to add AI literacy tools to its e-learning platform so entrepreneurs have clear, trustworthy guidance on using AI safely to grow their businesses.

AI is changing the way we work and do business, and small businesses deserve the tools to keep up and compete. I had a great conversation with my colleague @RepTroyDowning about our bipartisan AI-WISE Act, which helps small businesses harness this technology in a smart, responsible way.
Catch our discussion on @MeetThePress

If we can innovate in AI, we can also innovate in how we protect water resources, manage energy demand, and reduce environmental impacts. Policymakers must incentivize innovation that reduces environmental impacts of data centers, including closed-loop water systems, advanced cooling technologies, and clean-energy solutions that minimize strain on local infrastructure.
statements.venue: Planet Detroit voter guide candidate response

statements.text: West Michigan is stepping up to lead on responsible AI. This investment will help GVSU build the tools, partnerships, and research capacity needed to train the next generation of innovators, strengthen our workforce, and keep the U.S. competitive in emerging technologies. Proud to deliver resources that put our region at the forefront of smart, secure innovation.

Small businesses are the backbone of West Michigan, but too many owners are being asked to navigate rapidly changing technology without clear, reliable guidance. These bipartisan bills will support small businesses as AI reshapes our economy by ensuring Main Street has the same access to expertise and support as large corporations.
statements.venue: Press release on House passage of AI-WISE Act and AI for Main Street Act

statements.text: West Michigan entrepreneurs showed up, and today Congress delivered. My AI-WISE Act and AI for Main street Act passed the House with bipartisan support, giving small businesses access to the tools they need to grow and succeed. https://t.co/LyuwdLcfxq
I was energized to kick off the morning at ITI’s Tech Policy Summit breakfast discussing how AI can better serve small businesses. https://t.co/P8VQSWgNTy

I was proud to join Grand Valley State University to announce more than $1 million in federal funding I helped secure for the West Michigan Trustworthy AI Consortium. This investment will support cutting-edge research, strengthen our workforce, and ensure AI is developed responsibly, transparently, and with people at the center.

Artificial intelligence is no longer some far-off concept. It's here, and it's shaping our communities every single day in the products we manufacture, small businesses, delivery of health care and the training of our workforce. The question in front of us is not whether AI will change the future; it's how we can guide those changes thoughtfully.
statements.venue: Press briefing at GVSU, reported by MLive

statements.text: Trustworthy AI means building technology that is secure, reliable and transparent to consumers. It means asking hard questions about how automation affects workers, families and communities before the technology is deployed, not after.
statements.venue: Press briefing at GVSU, reported by MLive

statements.text:
I visited webAI today to meet with their team and learn more about the work they are doing right here in Grand Rapids. 
West Michigan is leading the way in ethical, secure AI, and I am excited to see that innovation happening in our community. https://t.co/jPnGKHKyQY

Proud to have @Google endorse my AI for Main Street Act and AI WISE Act.
These bipartisan bills will help connect small businesses with the tools and training they need to compete, grow, and keep up with a changing economy. It’s about making sure Main Street isn’t left behind.

I introduced the SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act to help modernize the Small Business Administration’s use of AI so it can reduce backlogs, streamline applications, prevent fraud, and better support Main Street businesses.
The government should be working smarter for the small businesses that keep our communities running.

The SBA can and should be using AI to reduce backlog, streamline applications for funding opportunities, and prevent fraud, which is why I requested this report in the first place and why it is critical we now implement its findings. As AI becomes an increasingly common part of our economy, we have to make sure Main Street businesses have the tools and support they need to grow, compete, and protect their operations.
statements.venue: Press release on SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act

statements.text: Entrepreneurs shouldn't be left behind as technology evolves. My AI-WISE Act helps connect small business owners with the AI training and resources they need to compete. https://t.co/nhY00M1mui

Tune in tomorrow at 7 PM for my conversation with Congressman Troy Downing. We covered everything from small businesses and AI to the issues shaping our communities. I hope you’ll join us! https://t.co/f23ql1mLFd

There’s nothing better than hearing directly from the people who make West Michigan work.
I visited Wolverine Worldwide employees talking about what’s on their minds, from AI and the future of work to affordability, trade, and protecting our Great Lakes. And of course, we couldn’t leave without stopping by the ReChaco facility to see their work firsthand!
Thanks for having me back, Wolverine!

AI is moving fast, and Congress is already behind.

From protecting our communities and families to making sure West Michigan businesses and workers can benefit from this technology, we need thoughtful, responsible solutions.

I’m focused on making sure AI is developed and used in a way that is safe and trustworthy.

I am proud to co-lead the Problem Solvers Caucus’s new AI working group. Congress has an urgent responsibility to establish regulations over artificial intelligence. While we can and should lead the world in AI development, we also must protect ourselves and hold the companies developing it accountable.
statements.quoted:
Today, the Problem Solvers Caucus Co-Chairs @RepBrianFitz and @RepTomSuozzi announced the formation of a new bipartisan working group focused on artificial intelligence and evolving technologies.
 
As artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies increasingly shape America, we are committed to advancing responsible policies that promote accuracy, transparency, and integrity in AI systems, while strengthening American competitiveness and protecting consumers, workers, and small businesses.
 
The working group will be led by @RepJoshG and @RepMikeLawler with @RepScholten and @RepBlakeMoore serving as vice leads.

statements.text: AI safety cannot wait. It’s time for Congress and global leaders to work together to ensure AI is regulated responsibly and for the good of humanity. https://t.co/0ocUgWOr3G

The rapid development of artificial intelligence and the recent, grave threats to our nation's cybersecurity are warning signs that cannot be ignored. I am working legislatively to make sure American people and businesses have the tools they need to understand AI and use it responsibly. I am honored to co-lead this crucial working group to exercise Congress's regulatory responsibility over the technology and establish much-needed guardrails. While we can and should lead the world in AI development, we also must protect ourselves and hold the companies developing it accountable.
statements.venue: Press release on co-leading Problem Solvers Caucus bipartisan AI working group

Join me for the third installment of my Congressional Dialogue Series on the Responsible Development of Artificial Intelligence.

October 5th, 2026 | 6-7PM

All are welcome, but registration is required for the safety and security of our guests. You can RSVP at https://t.co/ZRHKjvD5f6 to save your spot!

Thank you to everyone who joined us in person or tuned into yesterday’s Congressional Dialogue Series on artificial intelligence and data centers.

Technology is changing quickly, and we need to be ready to make critical decisions about how we build it. That’s why I’m bringing these conversations directly to West Michigan and giving your questions, concerns, and ideas a seat at the table in Congress.

I joined faith-based school leaders from across West Michigan for a roundtable discussion about the challenges facing their schools, from staffing and student needs to the growing use of AI in education.

Hearing directly from educators and school leaders helps me better understand the issues affecting students, families, and classrooms across our community. Thank you to Grand Rapids Christian Schools for hosting this important conversation.

Grand Valley State University and Van Andel Institute are bringing AI and biomedical research together to accelerate discoveries in the fight against diseases like cancer. Exciting work happening right here in our community!
https://t.co/kqqZcElOOE

Grand Rapids is becoming a hub for technology and innovation, and I was proud to help secure $1.031 million in federal funding for GVSU’s West Michigan Trustworthy AI Consortium.

As AI continues to evolve, we need to invest in research and education while making sure this technology is developed responsibly. That means protecting our privacy, keeping communities informed, and making sure small businesses and students have the tools to benefit from AI safely.

We can lead in innovation without sacrificing accountability, and I’m excited to see what this work brings to West Michigan.
